slides.texte_overlay:
how to deal with social
anxiety and make it less
present
Start with tiny, safe challenges. Say hello to a cashier, ask a stranger for the time. Small wins teach your brain that social moments are not dangerous.
Prepare one easy question for events. "How do you know the host?" Having something ready takes away the fear of standing there with nothing to say.
Focus outward, not inward. Notice the music, the room, the person in front of you. Anxiety grows when your attention is stuck on yourself.
Breathe out slowly before you walk in. A long exhale tells your body to calm down. Three slow breaths at the door can change how the next hour feels.
Keep your mind busy with good things. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and having curious thoughts leaves less room for worried ones.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Curious thoughts leave less room for worried ones.

slides.texte_overlay: Be kind to yourself after awkward moments. Everyone has them. Instead of replaying it all night, ask "What would I tell a friend?" and move on.
Talk to a professional if it limits your life. Social anxiety is common and very treatable. Asking for help is one of the strongest things you can do.
